name: Soil Moisture Variations
description: Soil moisture significantly impacts the speed of the robot on both paths. Path 2 (grass) will be slower on damp, compacted grass and faster on dry, loose grass. Path 1 (track) will be affected by moisture buildup or dryness impacting wheel traction. This is a highly likely explanation given the multimodal nature of the travel times.

name: Vegetation Density & Type (Path 2)
description: The density and type of grass between the crop rows on Path 2 will drastically change travel time.  Dense, tall grass will be much slower than sparse, short grass. Different grass types have varying consistencies and resistance. This is a primary driver of the variation.

name: Path 1 Surface Condition
description: The surface of the track (Path 1) – gravel, mud, loose soil, or compacted surface – will greatly influence robot speed. Variations in surface condition are highly likely to contribute to the multimodal distribution. It's assumed this changes over time.

name: Time of Day (Sun Angle/Shadows)
description: The sun's position and resulting shadows can affect camera performance and robot navigation.  Strong shadows could cause the robot to slow down or misinterpret the environment, particularly on Path 1, which might be more exposed to direct sunlight. This can indirectly impact speed.

name: Robot Wheel Slip/Traction
description: Variations in wheel slip due to uneven terrain, especially on Path 2, will dramatically affect travel time. This is directly related to soil moisture, but also to the robot’s wheel design and tire pressure.

name: Wind Speed & Direction
description: Wind can affect the robot's stability and potentially disrupt camera vision, particularly on Path 1. It can also cause issues with dust and visibility.

name: Crop Row Spacing & Orientation (Path 2)
description: The consistent spacing and orientation of crop rows on Path 2 will influence the robot's ability to navigate the gaps efficiently. Variations in these parameters can significantly alter travel time.

name: Robot Operational State (Battery Level)
description: As the robot’s battery degrades, it may reduce its speed to conserve energy, contributing to variations in travel time, particularly on longer journeys. This is an operational factor.

name: Camera Calibration Drift
description: Over time, camera calibration may drift, leading to inaccuracies in distance measurements and potentially affecting navigation and, consequently, travel time.  A sensor drift introduces systematic variation.

name: Maintenance Schedules (Track Wear)
description: The condition of the track (Path 1) changes due to maintenance, and changes in wheel wear, and this impacts travel speed. This represents a temporal, operational influence.

name: Presence of Small Obstacles
description: The robot will slow down or potentially get stuck on small obstacles (e.g., fallen leaves, small stones) that the camera might not fully detect or the robot’s navigation system might misinterpret, especially on Path 2.

name: Ambient Temperature
description: Extreme temperatures can affect the robot’s motor performance and wheel grip, impacting travel speed. Specifically, cold weather reduces wheel traction.

name: Lighting Conditions (Cloud Cover)
description: Changes in cloud cover impact the amount of light reaching the cameras, indirectly affecting their performance and navigation accuracy.

name: Robot Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) Drift
description: Drift in the IMU’s measurements will lead to accumulated errors in position estimation, affecting navigation and travel speed. This is a sensor error.

name: Field Slope/Terrain
description: Subtle variations in the terrain slope, particularly on Path 1, can alter the robot's speed and control, especially during turns. This is often a complex, combined effect of surface conditions.
